ai.text:
This bill moves responsibility for overseeing how foreign medical schools are accredited from the Department of Education to the Department of Health and Human Services. The work in question is done by the National Committee on Foreign Medical Education and Accreditation, which judges whether the accreditation standards used for foreign medical schools are comparable to those used for U.S. medical schools.

The bill transfers all of the Department of Education's powers and duties over this committee that it held before the bill takes effect. It also moves the staff and funding tied to these responsibilities to Health and Human Services. The bill notes that the Department of Education had already announced, on November 18, 2025, an agreement with Health and Human Services to help run the committee, including providing expertise, arranging meetings, and managing technology systems.

The bill gives the Office of Management and Budget a role in the transfer. That office must make sure the change does not increase the number of full-time equivalent employees at either department, and it must certify compliance with the bill to specified congressional committees.

Finally, the transfer does not affect any lawsuits, proceedings, or applications for benefits, services, licenses, permits, certificates, or financial assistance that are pending when the bill is enacted.

summary.text:
Less Bureaucracy, Better Foreign Medical Accreditation Act
This bill transfers specified functions relating to accreditation for foreign medical schools from the Department of Education (ED) to the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).
Specifically, the bill transfers to HHS all the functions and authorities exercised by ED before the bill's effective date related to the National Committee on Foreign Medical Education and Accreditation. (This committee evaluates the standards of accreditation applied to foreign medical schools and determines the comparability of those standards to standards applied to U.S. medical schools. On November 18, 2025, ED announced an interagency agreement with HHS for HHS to provide subject matter expertise, coordinate meetings, and manage technology systems to assist ED in managing and overseeing this committee.)
Additionally, the bill transfers to HHS all personnel and appropriations related to the functions that are transferred under this bill.
The bill outlines the authority of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) related to the functions that are transferred under this bill, including that OMB must ensure that this bill does not create a net increase in full-time equivalent employees at HHS or ED. Further, OMB must certify compliance with the bill to specified congressional committees.
The transfer of these functions does not affect any suits, proceedings, or applications for benefits, services, licenses, permits, certificates, or financial assistance that are pending on the date of this bill's enactment.
